findings.detail: Good, you're done. Now we get honey bread. There's a cart by the south arch that sells the good kind, and after a signing you deserve...
Then, half a second late, like a clerk thumbing through files to find your page... you.
Six years I chalked that woman's bouts and filed my shame under tradition. Now her name holds up the sky over three hundred roofs, and every soul in the Low Terraces says it when they point.
'Some of us have taken money on every fear this village ever had. If someone were to break the floor's bank for good, some of us would... find honest work. Slowly. With enormous complaining.'
Although. There was one supper. Aren stood up and said something about... water, I think. Water, or the fields, or...
'Some of us joined the survey to keep records, not to feed fires. If someone were to walk on the tower today, with the village behind them, some of us would countersign... slowly.'
'Stitching's poor,' he says at last, thickly. 'Whoever did that corner pulled the cord too tight. I'll redo it. I'll... we'll need a bigger banner, is what we'll need.'

'You don't return a file,' he manages. 'Returned means spent, means somebody's about to... what do you people want from me?' The whole market, listening from every shadow, holds its breath with him. Everyone here was raised on the same rule.
'It's smaller than I remembered,' he keeps saying, gripping the folder like a rail. 'Years I paid to keep this held, and it's... it's just a bad winter. It's just a man having a bad winter.'
The second lot? Frostfang, I said. Blue wool, wrist-marks. Why do you keep... I said that. Didn't I say that.

At dusk the seam parts on a slate of names, each beside the one thing its owner refused to cede. You read until the light goes and set it back. As the seam closes, a glyph surfaces beside your hand: the same cut that marks older acts of refusal, not a name or a Bloodline sign. Serel checks it against her staff. 'Same cut. Somebody saw you say no.'
A Legacy is not an ancestor coming back, and it is not something sleeping in a Bloodline. In the Sunken Court's age, people later called the Withheld refused to cede one defining choice.
...You asked twice. People keep asking me twice lately. I don't see why.
Witnesses use Legacy for a pattern someone chooses to repeat. It is not a Bloodline or an ancestor, and you may refuse the name.

Witnesses preserved accounts of what they did. Over time, they recognized a hundred recurring patterns of resistance. Those are the Legacies: deeds another person can choose to repeat. You don't inherit them from an ancestor.
No soul waits in that stone. The Gate is copying the recorded refusal and building a fighter from it. Stop the copy, then take a charcoal rubbing of the original mark for me.
The people you'll meet are memories preserved by the tower. They can speak and play their old decks, but their souls aren't trapped here.
That blank is a failed record, not a destiny. Drink from the cup, not the waterfall. Then tell me what matters before somebody else decides what it means.

Wandering Sage: Before you touch a seal, hear the terms plainly. You may accept one Legacy in your lifetime. It names a pattern in your deeds; no ancestor, soul, or Bloodline enters you.

Mira waits under the ridge gate with two coils over one shoulder and the weather slate under her arm. Objective: Choose the high cable line or the lower flower-picker road.
The old span hangs in two wet lengths above a narrow cut in the ridge. Objective: Rig the crossing with Mira's dry coil.
A fallen signal stone has split the high cairn, exposing a packet under its base. Objective: Recover Kesa's marker pieces and pressed flower.
The lower shelter leans into the ridge, its storm rail dragging loose in the wash. Objective: Repair the rail, then ask the picker crews about Kesa's marker.
Fresh runoff has opened the low cairn and left a waxed packet caught between its stones. Objective: Recover Kesa's marker pieces and pressed flower.
Conditional pages retain their trait gates.
Historical save without recorded field route.
Toma stands where the ash carts leave the village, a clamp bag in one hand and a folded oilcloth in the other. Objective: Choose whether to repair the footbridge first or follow the fresh cart trail.
The center plank has dropped below the handrail, and footprints still cross it in both directions. Objective: Fit Toma's offcuts and clamp the stringer before continuing.
Rainwater combs the channel reeds, and pale cedar edges show where the current has gathered them. Objective: Recover the scattered cedar plates without tearing their burned names.
Fresh cart ruts vanish among charcoal sledges, each runner black with the same ash. Objective: Find which cart carried the cedar plates toward the sluice.
The stopped sluice has caught a fan of black silt, bark, and pale cedar fragments. Objective: Recover and wrap the cedar plates, then return to the footbridge.
The recovered plates rest above the flood line while Toma sets a lamp beneath the failed span. Objective: Finish the bridge repair before returning the cedar plates.

Historical save without recorded field route.
Sova has set one lamp-oil jar between the wall watch and the lower-road cooks. Objective: Negotiate whether to divide the oil or keep the lower stove lit until dawn.
Three ridge lamps burn at half wick while the lower-road chimney gives one thin line of smoke. Objective: Pair the watch and kitchen crews for a low-light search.
Low lamps pick out waxed page edges where the gully folds toward the ridge. Objective: Recover the true roll pages with the paired crews.
The broth stove burns steadily while watchers, cooks, and families crowd around a map on the kneading table. Objective: Mark the storm's drift and organize a daylight search.
Morning throws thin shadows from waxed pages buried edge-up along the mapped lee. Objective: Recover the true roll pages in daylight.

Nyx waits beside a blank public notice while an unseen booth clerk watches from behind a shutter. Objective: Choose a protected source route or an open call for the ledger pages.
A decoy parcel waits on the east rail while one fresh wax thumbprint points west. Objective: Draw the buyer's watcher toward the decoy and follow the source's private mark.
A tarred parcel rests above the tide line, sealed with the booth clerk's witnessed mark. Objective: Recover the ledger pages and preserve the clerk's sealed account.

Nyx's wax-pattern notice hangs under the ferry lamp, surrounded by people pretending they stopped for the tide. Objective: Receive public page returns without claiming the protected clerk's testimony.
The abandoned booth is open on all sides, its counter covered in ledger pages and waiting witnesses. Objective: Reassemble the ledger under the public chain of custody.
